For `builtin_<library>` to work, you also need to place the following around audio library handling in `platform/linuxbsd/detect.py`:

```py
    if not env["builtin_opus"]:
		env["builtin_libogg"] = False # Needed to link against system opus
        env.ParseConfig("pkg-config opus --cflags --libs")
        env.ParseConfig("pkg-config opusfile --cflags --libs")
```

OK, I removed the constructor and destructor, which should be consistent if #118869 is merged.

Because `set_data` and `get_data` directly copy the data without any changes, it's better to use a `Vector` as it will just reference the given `p_data` and not allocate more memory for a copy.

```suggestion
	Vector<uint8_t> data;
```

This function is never called.

I get this was mostly made copying what `AudioStreamMP3` was at the time, but that one also got removed since destruction would clear it anyway.
Removed!
Is it a good idea to not copy here? Not copying means that if the data vector is modified elsewhere, it will modify the audio stream's data as well.

`Vector`s are mostly references. If two share the same data, and one of them wants to change, it will fork a copy of the original before doing so.

It would be a risk, however, if some piece of code got a const pointer to it and cast it to non-const, which bypasses copy-on-write and is a bad practice. But that doesn't happen here.

This would just make copying optional (in case you give an existing vector to `set_data`), instead of mandatory on every iteration.
